history.text: My partner says I'm controlling. I just like things done properly, and if I don't keep on top of the house and the money nothing gets done. I don't see why that makes me the bad guy.

1. You assume that "doing things **properly**" is a standard that can be universally applied.
2. You assume that if you do not **keep on top of** certain tasks, they will not happen.
3. You assume that being the person who ensures things get done makes you the **bad guy**.

Which of these stands out?
The one about doing things properly.
Because if I let go, things fall apart. I've seen it happen.
When you say things "fall apart," what specifically is happening?
What would Krishnamurti say about this?

I don't speak for anyone else; I only facilitate your own looking. 

What do you mean by "things fall apart"?
Honestly, isn't my partner the one with the problem here?

I cannot determine who has the problem. 

When you ask if your partner is the one with the problem, what are you looking for?
I suppose I've never really looked at what 'properly' means.
What would happen if things were done in a way that you didn't consider "proper"?
